subject.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API

question: Should after-compaction plugins receive a current-session reset method, and should official Codex/Copilot harness adapters receive the underlying raw deferred reset queue?
rationale: The public hook API and raw harness callback establish a durable plugin security boundary; source code alone cannot decide whether maintainers intend that authority to be public, bundled-only, or entirely core-owned.

options.title: Keep authority host-scoped
options.body: Expose only the current-session hook API and require a host-minted provenance capability for any official harness adapter that must enqueue resets.

options.title: Approve bundled raw authority
options.body: Allow official Codex/Copilot adapters to receive the raw queue after adding an immutable bundled-source identity check and explicit SDK documentation.

options.title: Keep resets core-owned
options.body: Remove the plugin reset method and have core compaction policy decide when a successful compaction rotates the session.

recommendation.title: Keep authority host-scoped
recommendation.body: Expose only the current-session hook API and require a host-minted provenance capability for any official harness adapter that must enqueue resets.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history shows direct ownership of the adjacent persisted-state compatibility decision and broad involvement in current lifecycle policy.
